task: Render an HTML composition to an MP4 video
packaging_note: Upstream's own render Dockerfile (packages/cli/src/docker/Dockerfile.render), built straight from the pinned Git context with the CLI version that commit declares (0.8.214)

access.why: The browser that renders your composition loads any fonts, images and scripts it links to from the web.

inputs.what: the composition: an HTML page whose root element has data-composition-id, data-start, data-duration, data-width and data-height, with GSAP timelines registered in window.__timelines under the composition id

known_issues: Upstream's Dockerfile declares ARG TARGETARCH=amd64, which wins even over --platform; without --build-arg TARGETARCH the arm64 build fetches an x86 ffmpeg and fails with a Rosetta 'failed to open elf' error
The composition loads GSAP from the jsdelivr CDN at render time, so rendering needs the network
Chromium needs --shm-size 1g; the image is about 3.4 GB
On arm64 under Docker Desktop the renderer reports 'BeginFrame did not run' and falls back to slower screenshot capture; a 3-second clip still renders in about 6 s and the output is correct

The renderer writes a .hyperframes/ folder beside the composition after each render; with the composition mounted read-only that step fails with ENOENT (the video is still written), so compose.yaml mounts it writable
